subject: Discovery recap: p95 SLA targets, streaming UX & concurrency constraints
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@fastchat.ai>, Ethan Morales <ethan@fastchat.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 SLA targets, streaming UX & concurrency constraints

Hi Olivia / Ethan —

Thanks again for the intro call today — appreciate you walking us through FastChat's real-time product and the scale you’re seeing. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, success criteria you called out, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I’ve missed.

Quick recap of pain points (as described by FastChat):
- End-user streaming latency: p95 hover ~700–900ms for multi-turn streaming responses; spikes during peak concurrency.
- Dropouts in streaming UX: intermittent websocket disconnects and token-level stalls during long responses.
- Concurrency pressure: bursts up to ~500 concurrent live sessions; average sustained concurrency ~180.
- Cost vs performance: current plan needs lower per-token cost at p95 target without worsening cold-starts.
- Measurement/telemetry gaps: team needs consistent p95/percentile metrics across regions and for streaming-specific metrics (time-to-first-byte token, TTFB-token).

Current stack (as described):
- Inference: self-hosted GPU fleet on cloud instances (G4dn-ish), batching layer yields high p50 but worsens tail.
- Orchestration: a custom proxy that does per-request batching; no unified KV prefix cache today.
- Streaming: websockets with chunked token frames; fallbacks to full response POST for some clients.

Success criteria FastChat called out:
- p95 latency for streaming responses <= 200ms for short/median responses (<= 32 tokens) and <= 350ms for longer streaming responses with progressive token emission.
- 99.9% availability SLA during business hours, with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model/region) under capacity stress.
- Maintain or reduce current cost per 1M tokens while achieving the latency targets.
- No loss of session continuity (zero or near-zero token drop during reconnect).

Redwood-specific recommendations / what we can run in the trial:
- Dedicated benchmark: we’ll run streaming-focused benchmarks with synthetic and recorded traffic (we suggest 48–72 hour window to capture peak patterns).
- Kernel/config suggestions: moderate quantization for larger models, continuous KV prefix cache for hot prompts, and tuned batching thresholds to avoid tail amplification.
- Streaming mode: support for WebSocket + chunk-level ACKs; configurable time-to-first-token optimization.
- Autoscale policy: burstable reserved capacity with warm standby to reduce cold-starts.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood to provision a 72-hour dedicated trial environment and baseline benchmark plan (attached bench-plan.xlsx). Target start: week of Jun 8.
2) FastChat to share a 60–90 minute sample trace (anonymized) and the top 10 prompt prefixes to seed prefix caching.
3) Align on p95 measurement definition (server-side token TTFB vs client-observed render latency).
4) Quick follow-up technical deep-dive with Marcus + engineering team (30–45 min) — propose Thu 6/4 10:00 PT.

Attachments: arch_diagram.png (high-level integration), SLA-draft_20260601.pdf (initial SLA language), bench-plan.xlsx (draft benchmark matrix).

If that looks right I’ll lock in the trial dates and route the NDA/SLA paperwork.

Thanks,

— Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Olivia Grant <olivia@fastchat.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ethan Morales <ethan@fastchat.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 SLA targets, streaming UX & concurrency constraints

Karthik —

Thanks for the thorough recap — yes, this aligns closely. A few clarifications on our side:

- Measured p95: we currently report p95 at the application layer (time from request to last token render). We can provide server-side trace logs as requested.
- Concurrency: peak bursts are short (~5–10 minutes) but repeat several times per hour. Peaks hit ~500 concurrent websocket sessions; average sustained concurrency ~150–200.
- Batching: our current batching window is 50–80ms and batch sizes average 24–32 in peak times; that’s where the tail gets worse.
- Security: SOC2 Type II in place; HIPAA is not a requirement today, but we do need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. Can Redwood support VPC + bring-your-own-KMS in the trial?

We can share an anonymized 48-hour trace and the top prefixes by tomorrow. The proposed 6/8 start for benchmarking works.

Also: for p95 targets you listed (<=200ms for short responses), that will be transformative for our UX — curious if you have data from similar streaming customers you can share (latency improvements post-redis cache / continuous batching changes).

I’ll accept the 6/4 technical deep-dive invite if that’s still open — Thu 10:00 PT works.

— Olivia
Head of Product | FastChat AI
olivia@fastchat.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Olivia Grant <olivia@fastchat.ai>, Ethan Morales <ethan@fastchat.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 SLA targets, streaming UX & concurrency constraints

Hi all — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

- Measurement: please confirm whether p95 is computed on per-session basis or across all requests; we prefer request-level percentiles with a separate session-resume metric.
- Streaming approach: Redwood supports WebSocket streaming and chunk ACKs; we’ll instrument time-to-first-token (server) and time-between-chunks (client) in the benchmark.
- Caching: prefix KV cache typically reduces p95 for repeated prefixes by 30–60% depending on prefix hit rate — we’ll include a cache warming pass.
- Autoscale: propose warm pool at ~30% of peak concurrency you expect during the window to limit cold starts.

A couple of questions for FastChat engineering: 
1) What is your TLS termination point today (LB vs app)?
2) Do you have request signatures / idempotency keys we should preserve when routing?
3) Which model variants are priority for the trial (smaller low-latency model + one high-quality model?), please list model names/weights.

I’ll bring a short demo of a streaming trace comparison (current vs Redwood baseline) to the Thu deep-dive.

— Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@fastchat.ai>, Ethan Morales <ethan@fastchat.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 SLA targets, streaming UX & concurrency constraints

Thanks everyone — quick logistics + next steps as we move toward the trial: 

Confirmed actions: 
- FastChat to share anonymized 48-hour trace + top-10 prefixes (Olivia) by 6/3 EOD.
- Redwood to provision a 72-hour dedicated trial starting 6/8; Marcus will circulate benchmark runbook and measurement definitions by EOD 6/5 (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-bench-plan).
- Security/legal: I’ll route the NDA and initial SLA draft to your legal team (attached SLA-draft_20260601.pdf); Vivek to follow up on VPC + KMS feasibility.
- Technical deep-dive: Thu 6/4 at 10:00 PT (30–45 min) — invite sent.

Benchmarks we’ll run (high level):
- Spike test: synthetic ramp to 600 concurrent websocket sessions for 10-minute windows to validate autoscale and tail behavior.
- Steady-state: 48-hour steady traffic replay at recorded concurrency distribution.
- Streaming quality: token-level TTFB, chunk gap distribution, token loss rate under reconnect.

Questions still open:
- FastChat: confirm model names/variants for the trial.
- FastChat legal: point of contact to receive SLA/NDA.
- Redwood: confirm exact warm-pool sizing once we see the trace.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the trial and ask our operations team to share access details and the temporary credentials for the benchmarking harness.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

— Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0191
